subject: Biotechnology
title: Biotech in Microgravity
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Biotech in Microgravity.

hook.text: Proteins form better crystals in space — microgravity eliminates convection currents that disrupt crystal growth on Earth.

buildup.text: Protein crystallography reveals molecular structure — better crystals mean sharper atomic maps for drug design.

discovery.text: Merck crystallized pembrolizumab in space — the space-grown crystals enabled a new subcutaneous formulation of the cancer drug.

twist.text: Launching experiments costs $20,000 per kilogram — space biotech must prove its products justify astronomical launch fees.

climax.text: SpaceX and Axiom Space make the ISS more accessible — commercial missions open space biotech to pharmaceutical companies.

punchline.text: Better drugs from zero gravity — space is biotech's most expensive laboratory.

quiz.question: Why do proteins form better crystals in microgravity?
options: Microgravity eliminates convection currents that disrupt crystal growth, allowing larger and more uniform crystals
The vacuum of space removes water from protein solutions faster
